facts.statement: The type species S. yaoi was described by Chung Chien Young in 1944.
facts.quote: The type species, S. yaoi, was described by Chung Chien Young, in 1944.

facts.statement: Originally thought to be an ornithopod ornithischian, the specimen was reclassified as a sauropod in 2016.
facts.quote: Initially reported by Young as an ornithopod ornithischian, this specimen was unambiguously referred to Sauropoda in 2016 by McPhee et al.

facts.statement: Later studies refined its position to a basal gravisaurian, closely related to Vulcanodon and Tazoudasaurus.
facts.quote: later refined to a basal gravisaurian position by Pol et al. in 2020 and 2022, closely related to Vulcanodon and Tazoudasaurus.

facts.statement: Sanpasaurus lived during the mid-Jurassic, approximately 165 to 161 million years ago, between the Bathonian and Callovian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 165 y 161 millones de años, entre el Bathoniense y Calloviense

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the Ziliujing Formation in Kuangyuan, Sichuan province, China.
facts.quote: Encontrado en la Formación Ziluijing, en las series de Kuangyuan, provincia de Sichuan, China.

facts.statement: The describer noted that the remains arrived mixed at the laboratory, making the association of bones uncertain.
facts.quote: quien reconociera los restos que legaron mezclados al laboratorio, por lo que la asociación de estos no es definitiva.

facts.statement: Sanpasaurus belongs to the order Saurischia.
Sanpasaurus is classified within the suborder Sauropoda.
The Paleobiology Database records the time range for Sanpasaurus as the Toarcian, from 184.2 to 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 174.7 million years ago)
